title: Stabilize FP8 activation variance clamp + per-batch norm for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Enabling FP8 profiles on Hopper (E4M3/E5M2) shows nondeterministic activation saturation on a small fraction of real traffic leading to time-limited accuracy regressions. Root cause analysis points to per-batch activation variance spikes and rare outlier tokens that push quantization ranges. This ticket implements a two-pronged runtime mitigation and calibration update: 1) a runtime 'variance_clamp' layer that limits per-layer per-batch activation scale changes driven by exponential moving estimate; and 2) a lightweight per-batch normalization pass (activation rescale) applied only during quantization path to reduce tail events. The approach aims to preserve token-level latency SLOs while reducing calibration sensitivity and enabling broader E4M3/E5M2 profile activation without aggressive fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Enabled FP8 profiles (E4M3/E5M2) on two Hopper rings with variance_clamp + per-batch normalization without increasing P50 latency by >5%
No more than 0.5% of requests in the shadow canary show accuracy regression > 1.5% on golden prompt set A (LLM-completion regression metric)
Automated calibration pipeline runs end-to-end and produces stable quantization params (std dev < 3% across 5 runs) for target models: rw-13b and rw-57b
Rollout plan + rollback hooks documented and sign-off from SRE and Applied ML
Observed reduction in activation overflow telemetry (overflow_count metric) by >= 90% in canary compared to baseline FP8 activation runs
implementation_notes: Add runtime flag --fp8-variance-clamp (default: 0.15) to cap per-batch scale change relative to EMA; tune per-model during calibration
Implement optional lightweight per-batch rescale transform applied only to tokens entering quantizer; gated behind model-profile config
Calibration pipeline: add a post-calibration consistency step that runs 3 short micro-evals across diverse prompts and rejects profile if regression exceeds threshold
Telemetry: emit fp8.activation_variance, fp8.variance_clamp_applied, fp8.overflow_count, fp8.per_batch_rescale_pct for dashboarding
Performance: microbench indicates per-batch normalization adds ~0.6ms per request for rw-57b on 80-token sequences — acceptable for P1 but may need optimization for low-latency tiers
Fallback: if variance_clamp triggers >10% of batches for 10m window, auto-fallback to int8-compatible profile with alerting

notes_on_tradeoffs: Aggressive variance clamping reduces quantization failures but can mask model distribution shifts — mitigated by keeping clamp conservative and surfacing metric when clamp is active
Per-batch normalization solves tail events but adds CPU cost; chosen as opt-in per-tier to avoid impacting hosted SLO without customer opt-in
Calibration guard increases calibration runtime slightly (extra micro-evals) but prevents bad profiles from reaching production
